resources.string: Project an Android phone over a USB cable or wirelessly. Not yet tested on every phone and head unit.
No head-unit identity is installed, so Android Auto cannot connect. docs/ANDROID_AUTO.md explains how to add one to a personal build.
Last connection: %1$s s from plug-in to the first picture.
Start when an Android phone is plugged in
Switches the phone to Android Auto and opens it with no tap, whether this app is open or not. Android asks once which app to use; choose this one and “Always”.
When Android Auto drops while the phone stays plugged in, connect again after 1, 2, 4, 8 and 15 seconds. A refused USB prompt or identity is not retried.
Applies at the next Android Auto connection. Automatic picks the largest size this screen shows sharply.
How large Android Auto draws text and buttons. Higher is larger. Applies at the next Android Auto connection.
60 fps is smoother on a fast head unit and heavier on a slow one. Applies at the next Android Auto connection.
Their own streams let the car mix directions over music. Choose the media stream if a head unit plays only that one. Applies at the next Android Auto connection.
Android Auto puts its controls on the driver’s side set in %1$s → %2$s.

Head unit sends this unit’s own GPS to Android Auto, which helps where the phone’s reception is poor; it needs precise location. Phone keeps the phone’s own GPS. Applies at the next Android Auto connection.
Saved. It applies at the next Android Auto connection.
Start when a known phone connects over Bluetooth
Starts wireless Android Auto with a phone that has used it here before; connect it once with Connect wirelessly. Uses the Wi-Fi set up for wireless CarPlay, or else Wi-Fi Direct.
Wireless Android Auto needs Nearby devices or Location to reach the phone. Allow them in this app’s permissions.
